W1.name: representation
W1.rule_restated: the representation cannot alter the frozen production semantics, acceptance criteria, length ladder or measurement definitions

a_adopted_rows_draining_front.what: per layer a Vec of adopted K rows and one of V rows plus a base; after appending p, drain every row below HistoryRange.required_start(p)
a_adopted_rows_draining_front.view: KvView::rows_from(base, …) — the static Rows backing (V2's fast path)
a_adopted_rows_draining_front.row_data_copied_per_append: none: the backend's row is adopted, as row/v1 does
a_adopted_rows_draining_front.release: each dropped row's own allocation freed as it is drained — witnessable on allocation identity (address + adoption generation)
a_adopted_rows_draining_front.cost: a memmove of ≈ w row pointers (24 B each, ≈24 KB) per sliding layer per append

b_adopted_rows_in_a_ring.what: VecDeque of adopted rows; pop_front is O(1)
b_adopted_rows_in_a_ring.view: a VecDeque is not contiguous, and rows(&self) cannot make_contiguous; needs a Dyn KvRows wrapper (dynamic dispatch per row read)

c_contiguous_ring_of_copied_rows.what: w rows × kv_dim preallocated per sliding layer; each appended row copied into its slot, the incoming Vec freed
c_contiguous_ring_of_copied_rows.view: wraps around, so not linear from base: Dyn or a two-segment view
c_contiguous_ring_of_copied_rows.row_data_copied_per_append: one row (the store traffic canonical/v1 pays)
c_contiguous_ring_of_copied_rows.complexity: largest: wrap-around indexing, and full-span layers still need a growing store

W1.decision: (a) adopted rows with a draining front
W1.reason: the smallest representation that meets every frozen condition: exact base/end, physical release of each dropped row witnessable on its own allocation identity, no second authority, zero row-data copies, and the static Rows view backing. (b)'s O(1) removal saves a pointer memmove that is a secondary cost, at the price of dynamic dispatch on every row read; (c) adds a copy per append and wrap-around indexing. Their allocator and throughput differences are secondary observations and are not measured as a comparison here.
W1.not_the_proof_provider: (a) shares the SHAPE of VIEW-1 V4's ExactRetention, which was a test instrument; window/v1 is written fresh as production code in larql-kv (vindex3/window.rs), with its own identity, factory and documentation, and without the proof provider's check log or seeding hooks
W1.identity_and_regions: identity `window/v1`, registered in shipped_continuations beside row/v1 and canonical/v1; declares ONLY the Kv region, so a plan needing Recurrent or LatentKv is refused at selection (frozen scope)
W1.fixed_representation_capacity_declared: per layer, the two row-list (Vec<Vec<f32>>) buffers: on a sliding layer their length never exceeds w + 1 (the appended row before the drain), so after warm-up their capacity stops growing — the only provider-born storage; every row allocation is adopted. W3 checks post-window growth of sliding-layer live K/V bytes against exactly this.
W1.full_span_layers: HistoryRange::Full: base stays 0 and nothing is drained — identical storage behaviour to row/v1
